# DiagonalLinePath { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath }

```python
loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath(start, end, tolerance=10.0)
```

Time axis as a diagonal (arbitrary straight) line.

Useful for rotated segments, skewed timelines, or any straight
line that isn't perfectly horizontal or vertical.

The timeline coordinate maps to arc length along the line,
so length equals the Euclidean distance between endpoints.

## Attributes {.doc-section .doc-section-attributes}

| Name      | Type                                                   | Description                                |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| start     | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[float](`float`), [float](`float`)\] | (x, y) starting point.                     |
| end       | [tuple](`tuple`)\[[float](`float`), [float](`float`)\] | (x, y) ending point.                       |
| tolerance | [float](`float`)                                       | Distance tolerance for from_2d conversion. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}

```python
>>> path = DiagonalLinePath(start=(0, 0), end=(300, 400))
>>> path.length  # sqrt(300^2 + 400^2) = 500
500.0
>>> path.to_2d(250)  # Halfway point
(150.0, 200.0)
```

| Name | Description |

```python
loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath.distance_to_path(x, y)
```

### from_2d { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath.from_2d }

```python
loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath.from_2d(x, y)
```

Map (x, y) to timeline coordinate.

Projects the point onto the line and returns the arc length
if the projection falls within the segment.

### to_2d { #timetoalign.loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath.to_2d }

```python
loader.graphical.DiagonalLinePath.to_2d(coord)
```

Map timeline coordinate (arc length) to (x, y).
